facts.raw_span: 48-year-old white man
lifelong non-smoker
remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid 17 years earlier
three-month history of mild hemoptysis
cough without dyspnea
non-tender, 2 × 2 cm subcutaneous mass on his left forearm
oxygen saturation of 94% on room air
normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count, liver and renal function tests, and coagulation profile
polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region adjacent to the anterior wall on chest CT scan
mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall just above the main carina, causing an 80% obstruction of the right main bronchus and 70% obstruction of the left main bronchus on flexible bronchoscopy
tumor consisted of large nests of eosinophilic cells within a collagenous and myxoid matrix on hematoxylin–eosin staining
carcinoid tumor was initially suspected

concepts.why: The patient has a history of a remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid and now presents with a polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region, which is consistent with a tracheal carcinoid tumor.
The patient has a mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall, which could be a tracheal adenoma, although the histological features are more suggestive of a carcinoid tumor.
The patient has a non-tender subcutaneous mass on his left forearm, which could be a metastasis from the tracheal tumor, although the primary tumor type and the metastatic site are not typical.
The patient has a polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region, which could be a tracheal papilloma, although the clinical and histological features are more suggestive of a carcinoid tumor.

rationales.F03: History of tracheal carcinoid resection increases likelihood of tracheal carcinoid tumor and subcutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F10: Mass arising from the tracheal wall with significant obstruction is more typical of tracheal carcinoid tumor or tracheal adenoma.
rationales.F11: Tumor histology showing large nests of eosinophilic cells within a collagenous and myxoid matrix is highly suggestive of tracheal carcinoid tumor.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of a remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid and the current tumor's histological features, including large nests of eosinophilic cells within a collagenous and myxoid matrix, strongly support this diagnosis.
